[h2]TL;DR; A decent twinstick shooter roguelike that needs a bit more polish[/h2] [i]For some context, I'm a UX and UI designer, I've been in the industry for 15+ years. I'll be reviewing some of the gameplay, and mostly focus on the interface and experience as that seems to be a big pain point to a lot of other reviewers. I'm not here to ♥♥♥♥ on someone's hard work, just give honest feedback.[/i] Honestly, a great start for their first game. I think it nails most of the fundamentals of twinstick shooter roguelikes. [h3]The Good Things[/h3] [olist] [*]Guns are varied, feel and sound different [*]Characters have different basic stats and are visually unique to one another [*]Equipment mixes the game a bit [*]Single-use buffs give a reason to spend your credits [*]The hub is a practice area to test weapons before purchasing them [*]The arena is a set amount of space, meaning it will get claustrophobic [/olist] [h3]The Odd Choices[/h3] [olist] [*]There are three different fonts used. Two are pixel and in-game, the third is the main and pause menu [list] [*]General rule is to use a unique font for headers and a readable font for general text [/list] [*]The scoreboard uses a different screen and platform, it's a bit jarring [*]Pressing Escape in a screen/sub-menu, closes it but also opens the pause menu [*]Flashlight seems a little underbaked, or the mechanic isn't strong enough [list] [*]Visually I can see the enemies outside the radius. I understand it's tied to having passives and skills that affect enemies inside the light [*]I'd suggest looking at Disfigure or 20 minutes till Dawn's light radius mechanic. Are you aiming to hide the enemies for a fear effect or obscure vision? [/list] [*]The placement of the stats during a level-up [list] [*]Skills are on the left and text/stats are on the right. Generally, Western audience, read from left to right. Having the text on the right makes it more difficult to read (at an efficiency level). Moving the layout around would help [*]I say Western audience, as there's no option to choose a language when starting the game. So the assumption is that English will be read from left to right [/list] [*]Enemy design is there but sort of melts into one another [list] [*]Their colours are usually red, green and dark grey. They look different but they also just meld into another another after a while [*]Having looked at Pen's portfolio, they do amazing pixel art. The game art is still great but just seems to miss that extra flair that makes things stand out more [/list] [/olist] [h3]The Bad Things[/h3] [olist] [*]When purchasing new characters, guns, equipment; the price obscures the text and the opacity decreases readability [list] [*]People just want to know what they're purchasing first before making the jump. Yes, you can read it if you really squint your eyes and look harder, but don't make users work for it [/list] [*]UI for the boss health takes a chunk of the bottom [list] [*]To alleviate it, the opacity of the bar fades as your character moves down. That works, but not all the information is present for the player to make an informed decision whether or not they should move downwards. Often then, they take damage running down blind. It just feels unfair [/list] [*]The UI during gameplay feels too large, or there is too much irrelevant information [list] [*][h3]At [b]first glance[/b], top-left UI:[/h3] [*]The EXP bar is barely noticeable, the text at top center is not readable until the bar is filled halfway [*]The stats read, from left to right: Health, some blue thing, grey percentage, exclaimation percentage, purple percentage, red percentage [*]After 80+ min of playing, I know the stats read as: Health, some blue thing, defense, crit chance, purple percentage, and blood/rage [*]Ammo UI is repeated at the top-left and by your character [*]Skill UI: the skill icon of the default character looks like a 5, next to skill uses, can be confusing. The current character should be enough as a visual marker as to what skill they would have [/list] [*]The use of icons instead of text in the skill and endgame stat screens [list] [*]In terms of user experience, you are making users do extra work by highlighting the icon to then read. Icons are not universally understood across, so having some clarity might help as well [/list] [*]Timer is okay to have, but the score doesn't. During a level-up screen, there is an option to choose a multiplier, I think from there it is more relevant [/olist] Overall, I really enjoy the game. It's a really great start for their first game, it just needs some refining to get everyone on-board. Thanks for taking the time to reading this feedback/review.

Looks: great! Control: good/great Performance: excellent from what I've seen, can't speak for end-game Fun: okayish UI: confusing and sometimes hard to read Affordability: fantastic Replayability: very low The progression system needs a rework. After a few games I got bored, already having unlocked quite a few things and left with no goals to achieve. Sure I could unlock more but it didn't feel those unlocks would be better or sufficiently interesting compared to what I already had. Bullet hell games shine for me when things go up to 11 after the grind. Here it seems you just (cheaply) buy some combination of weapon/skill and try to find the right builds and get a bit of luck during your run. Only if you like bullet hell games pure for the skill and don't care much about progression I would recommend it in it's current state. Otherwise; it's cheap and you'd be supporting a small developer but don't expect to get a lot of mileage out of your purchase. I'll be hoping for some improvements that make playing it more rewarding.

I absolutely adore mr Penusbmic artstyle and purchased the game mainly to support him a bit. What I received is more than what I've expected. The gameplay feels smooth, characters and weapons I've unlocked up until this point feel unique, the game is just fun. Progression is simple, but that's not necessarily a bad thing - I enjoyed being able to unlock things as I see fit. If I'm required to give some feedback, settings menu would benefit from some rework. Using my settings (75% windows sound volume level) 25% in-game sound level feels way too high, and the only way to lower the sound volume is via windows sound mixer (the game has only 0/25/50/75/100% settings). Also, in-game explanation display rotates in fixed speed, making the first reading fairly awkward. The leaderboard style looks really plain and disconnected from the rest of the game. Most of negatives affect only first 15 minutes after launching the game for the first time and the gameplay is really fun - imo it's just a good purchase at this price point.

Half the time something stabs me when I can't see it until it's right next to me. I barely beat normal, and higher difficulties feel like you need meta upgrades... that just aren't there. There isn't any skill involved here. You walk around, hope not to be surrounded, and if you don't complete a run you barely get any resources to get more unlocks.While I can appreciate the horizontal progression, it makes me feel like I don't care enough to get more unlocks since I'd just pick what I like and stick to it. Poison isn't interesting, it's just a DoT like fire. The choices you have at base make more meaningful decisions than in game. I typically go synergy with current build > reload/fire speed > damage as my progression. Most poison unlocks are useless unless you have a poison gun or poison ability since you don't get anything baseline. Fire typically gives you something along with it. People are saying this needs more polish, but I don't see Early Access slapped on so I don't know if the dev is gonna keep working on it. I'm not refunding a 5 dollar game, but could be better.

It's a really fun way of getting into both the Roguelike and Bullet Hell genres. The controls are simple, and it has some of the "deck-building" aspects of games like Slay the Spire. The core of the fun is creating synergies between your chosen weapon, chosen character, and power-ups acquired during runs. Some of the synergies are definitely more fun than others (stationary and "pet" builds are super fun once they get going), but each one has its own appeal. With more updates, specifically more power-ups, this game could quickly get to the point where every run truly feels different, which would take it to the next level. penusbmic is also one of the best game development asset creators out there, so make sure to check out their sprites!

One of the best roguelikes out there. It's like Brotato on a smaller scale. It doesn't have a lot of content if you don't go for all achievements, but if you do - it's a blast and it's difficult enough to not get bored replaying the same content. The way you can combine weapons, characters and passive skills to complete a 500 second run is great. There are a lot of different combos that actually work. Gameplay is very enjoyable and doing "one more run" is never exhausting.

Fun game, but very limited and the bugs are pretty frustrating. * Some guns can get perks that give them more crit chance but it doesn't apply the crit chance at all. * The armor and dodge stats seemingly diminish during endless, which is fine, but it's not described anywhere. * If you kill a boss outside of the arena you can't pick up the drops, but they seem to still be rendered because they appear briefly when you level up * The power up that gives you damage per xp seems to work exponentially to the point where if you have 200+ xp you can reach an integer overflow and technically have negative damage * Endless mode stops spawning bosses maybe after 1500 seconds? Or maybe because I couldn't pick up their drops? * There seems to be a limit on the magnet width that I reached, but it's impossible to know if it wasn't increasing. Just felt like it wasn't. * Some times power ups show which mastery they contribute to and some times they don't. Unclear what causes this, but it happens pretty often. I would really like it if there were more enemies and more power ups. Maybe a way to block certain power ups? Extraction mode gets to a point where your only limit is boredom. The enemies don't seem to get more health or speed after maybe 1000 seconds. I gave up at about 45 minutes Also a description of how blood/pain damage works would be helpful. Are they the same thing?

Received it as gift from my partner, it was a very nice gift imo ❤❤❤ Pretty challenging and fun, lots of build options, I enjoy it as a warm-up or cooldown before or after a larger match in another game, also as disassociation device (with certain chill builds) or just a when taking a small break [spoiler] since the max time a normal, hard or insane run will take is 500 sec. :D [/spoiler] It's a 7/10 bang for buck in my opinion.

The game is not bad overall, a lot of effort has been put into it, but there are some issues that prevent me from fully enjoying it. Firstly, there are bugs. The crit ability does not work on the Bone Barrel, even though I reported it back in September. The developers have ignored this issue. Secondly, the dark level are awful, and the game already demands a certain level of skill, but playing through these level can be extremely frustrating and stressful. I'm sure many have abandoned the game at this point, but the developer doesn't care if he doesn't care, then the assessment will be appropriate.

I tried to like it but it's just not very fun. It's also way too hard to see what's going on in harder levels due to the graphic design choice. Also enemies move way too fast and even with the fastest characters you feel like your walking through quicksand and there are no upgrades for speed that I've seen except ones that make you go even slower.

It is just not really fun. The enemies are impossible to see even with the "highlight enemies" setting on which works for some enemies. There is a auto aim mode you can enable which is helpful but sometimes the game just crashes when you try to open the settings menu which voids your run. The UI is a mess, most of the time I have no idea what I'm looking at. It also doesn't really have that much to do with bunnies. Like in Kitty survivors you have upgrades about cats like a yarn ball etc. in this game there is no such thing. Also bunnies are supposed to be fast but your character always feels slow and sluggish. The game is extremely bad at explaining stuff. Like an upgrade can say "x will scale with y" but it wont say the factor so it can be that x now deals 0.001y more. Also when you level up you can choose between 3 upgrades and a multiplier for your score which is nice and unique but I don't know what my score does so I don't really know in which scenario picking that would be useful. Overall it is just a mess and it doesn't feel nice. If I could refund the game I would buy 20 minutes till dawn to one of my friends.

AWESOME! The feeling you get when you do a poison build and finally beat the boss you were stuck on. MUAH! The game is awesome and looking forward to playing more! Penusbmic crushed this one! Here is some gameplay before release: https://youtu.be/lB53okVvVKQ

TLDR: its fun and given its not very expensive, its worth picking up. I wont bother going over the mechanics of the game itself, as they are fairly straight forward and the game doesn't really have much depth past them. The game loop is fairly straight forward, do runs, get coins/items, buy Heroes, buy items, buy guns, repeat. At the start this was pretty engaging, as you can also unlock weapon perks, and work towards the character upgrade, etc. Once I started getting a decent amount of weapons and Heroes unlocked (along with items and consumables) I tried the 'Hard mode' (second mode out of five) and it kicked my butt. It took me several tries to complete a run, by which time I was using some of the mid game weapons and characters, but found that these are not actually that much powerful than the initial Heroes or weapons, bar 1 weapon and 1 character, Zeppelin and Nikki. I was expecting, given the score based nature of the end modes, that weapons (and to a lesser extent, Heroes) would get, at least, decently stronger than the weapons that game before them, but I found that this was not the case. I found that the later weapons would have only a little better damage, but not by a lot, and the unique traits that came with them were not that strong making some weapons almost unusable unless you get perfect luck in the power ups that you get. I found this quite frustrating, as runs could very easily be decided by luck on hard and, in some cases, normal depending on the weapon, when I felt like the later weapons should give you a decent leg up even if you get bad power up luck. This brings me to be crux of the issue with this game, balance. I have put ~12 hours into this game so far, however, I don't feel that much stronger then when I did when I started the game. For me, the Insane mode is easier than the hard mode, as the first boss, The Phantom, is quiet a bit easier than the Collector. I was looking forward to using the later weapons, but I have been disappointed by all of the later weapons when using them. I have yet to really play much of the Dark mode or Endless yet, but I cant see the experience being that different from what I have encountered. I'm not really sure what the point of all the cool weapons (interesting unique traits and damage styles) is if they don't increase the power fantasy. I would love to see a decent power gradient between the initial weapons and the latter ones, so that you want to unlock them. I don't feel like the heroes need to be changed in functionality, as they do bring interesting play styles to the game, but I would like to see them have less uses and instead have a greater impact when using the 'alt'. With the lack of weapon progression, they can be annoying when they don't feel that impactful. I really enjoy the art style and game flow, so am hoping the above can be addressed to improve the experience and replay value.

4/10 Unpolished, unbalanced, and small content. Zero control on the power ups (no ban, save for later, you just get the full pool of rng, kinda annoying for building up..) And progression doesn't feel good. It's decent for the genre, but there are better games.

[b]Edit:[/b] 75 powerups may seem like a lot, but for roguelikes/roguelites/survivors games, this number is extremely small. No matter how uniquely they are designed, you can encounter most of them in the 1st run and then they become increasingly boring... Challenging, enjoyable in its own way, but I still dislike it: - after 10 runs, powerups/level-up-skills become boring and repetitive, especially since you can't disable some of them like in other horde survivors games, and there is no greater variety to them - endless mode is hard to unlock - the map is extremely small, claustrophobic - no grind for passives or nicer upgrades to main weapons (there are only 3 weap upgrades) makes every run as hard as before, sapping energy after numerous runs rather than being more enjoyable - no pet variety - only expensive consumables, no passive skills / anything except chars/weapons that carry on Merits + challenging + okay variety of monsters/enemies + nice combat dynamic + balanced enough

It's pretty good. I found myself just holding down the fire button tho, so an auto-attack option would be nice. I set one up using a macro, but I'd prefer it if the developers just saved me a minute by doing that for me.
save the $5, it isn't bad, it's just mediocre.

Extremely basic Survivors-style game. You're placed on a small rectangle arena without any obstacles, random enemies spawn, you kill them, you collect their dropped EXP, you level up, you pick 1 of 3 random upgrades, and repeat the process until you survive for 500 seconds. That's the whole gameplay. An overwhelming majority of the upgrades are boring mechanics that you've seen in millions of other games before. "Your bullets now apply poison", "summon a turret", "gain crit chance", "enemies have a chance to explode", "heal every few seconds", "gain a regenerating shield", "drop a bomb on reload", things like that. The only couple of interesting mechanics are "Hero Light", which is the light surrounding your character and inflicting Slow or Burn with specific upgrades; and "Blood Damage", which... I'm not really sure what it does? but it fades away over time, and has upgrades tied to it that bump it back up. The upgrades aren't balanced well either. The game's Hard difficulty is basically impossible to pass if you pick anything other than AoE damaging upgrades early on, severely limiting the potential build variety. I mean, if I'm getting overwhelmed by 20 enemies existing on the screen at the same time, why would I pick a turret that shoots one enemy at a time or poison that doesn't make me shoot more bullets? Of course I'd rather go for the upgrades that let me clear the hordes. Some enemies feel too bullet spongy for what they are - there's one that periodically creates a large shield circle around itself, blocking ALL your bullets from damaging anything inside of it, and one that follows your horizontal movement and shoots a vertical laser from the top of the screen every 4 seconds. The combat music track, while seeming fine at first, gets old after listening to it on loop for 2-3 runs. The artstyle is good - this game [i]was[/i] made by the artist on [i]Dome Keeper[/i] and [i]Shogun Showdown[/i] after all. Overall, I don't feel satisfied with Bullet Bunny. I would rather play a different Survivors game that actually tries to put its own unique spin on the formula.

Personally, I think it's ok but it has a lot of pain points that are enough for me to say that it's a lot less desirable in the genre it's at. - names and descriptions of skills sometimes barely make sense, for example, as far as I remember, there's something called "bullet-proof" but it increases your bullet damage instead, which was odd. - very limited enemy variety. The enemies shown in the trailer is like what, 90% of the enemy types total? [strike] Granted I haven't checked the last 2 difficulties [/strike] (yea basically the same enemies). - exp vanishing if you don't pick it up in time isn't a fun mechanic. Not really a big deal considering the map size but it gets annoying nonetheless. - the weapons and characters aren't engaging at all. More often than not, the very basic pistol is the more reliable choice than even the expensive ones. Yes, even on the higher difficulties. - elemental synergies might as well not exist because of how underwhelming they perform even when stacked. Just do raw damage. - overall feel is incomplete. It tried to merge bullet hell and survivor-like genre but wasn't good at both. Good potential tho. would've used a side thumb but it doesn't exist so I'm leaning towards thumbs down for this atm.
No raccoons. Rogue-like bullet hell. Survive the timer with numerous characters, power ups, gems, and guns. Decent amount of customization in early access and more to come post launch.
